# Releases
## @swisspost/design-system-components@10.0.0-next.49

### Major Changes

-   Removed support for multiple links in the `post-linkarea` component; it now throws an error if more than one link is detected in the slotted content. (by [@leagrdv](https://github.com/leagrdv) with [#6324](https://github.com/swisspost/design-system/pull/6324))

### Minor Changes

-   Added a new component-names.json file, which contains a list of all components the package is outputting. (by [@oliverschuerch](https://github.com/oliverschuerch) with [#6199](https://github.com/swisspost/design-system/pull/6199))

### Patch Changes

-   Added styles to highlight the current navigation item marked with `aria-current="page"` and its potential parent item in the header main navigation. (by [@myrta2302](https://github.com/myrta2302) with [#6216](https://github.com/swisspost/design-system/pull/6216))

-   Updated the `<post-accordion-item>` component to enforce a top border in all use cases. (by [@hugomslv](https://github.com/hugomslv) with [#6151](https://github.com/swisspost/design-system/pull/6151))

-   Fixed accessibility issue in the `<post-breadcrumbs>` component by wrapping breadcrumb items in `<li>` elements. (by [@alionazherdetska](https://github.com/alionazherdetska) with [#6294](https://github.com/swisspost/design-system/pull/6294))

-   Fixed the `post-header` component to consistently omit the title container when no title is defined across all configurations. (by [@alizedebray](https://github.com/alizedebray) with [#6244](https://github.com/swisspost/design-system/pull/6244))

-   Refactored icon path to improve readability and maintain correct handling of multiple sources. (by [@myrta2302](https://github.com/myrta2302) with [#6220](https://github.com/swisspost/design-system/pull/6220))

-   Improved `<post-avatar>` markup and added a `description` prop to allow users to provide additional context to the component. (by [@myrta2302](https://github.com/myrta2302) with [#6092](https://github.com/swisspost/design-system/pull/6092))

-   Updated `<post-menu>` and `<post-menu-item>` to prevent accessibility roles from being announced before the menu content is visible, and to ensure correct focus behavior on menu items during keyboard navigation when NVDA is running.  
    Removed the obsolete `role="menuitem"` from `<post-language-switch>. `<post-language-option>`now assigns`role="listitem"`in case of`variant="list"\`, to ensure a correct reference relationship.

    Updated the `<post-breadcrumbs>` component by removing an `aria-label` set on the trigger wrapper `<div>`, which was causing an accessibility error. Also added `role="none"` to the wrapper div to reflect its presentational purpose. (by [@myrta2302](https://github.com/myrta2302) with [#6042](https://github.com/swisspost/design-system/pull/6042))

-   Updated dependencies:
    -   @swisspost/design-system-icons@10.0.0-next.49
    -   @swisspost/design-system-styles@10.0.0-next.49

## @swisspost/design-system-components-angular@10.0.0-next.49

### Major Changes

-   Updated Angular components to output as standalone components to align with Angular 20's default approach where components are standalone by default, eliminating the need to declare them within NgModules. Developers using our components should replace `PostComponentsModule` imports with `providePostComponents()` in their app providers and import individual components (e.g., `import { PostIcon, PostButton } from '@swisspost/design-system-components-angular'`) for standalone use.  
    BEFORE:

    ```typescript
    // app.module.ts
    @NgModule({
      imports: [
        PostComponentsModule,
      ],
    })
    ```

    AFTER:

    ````typescript
    //app.module.ts
    @NgModule({
      providers: [
        providePostComponents(),
      ],
    })
    ``` (by [@alionazherdetska](https://github.com/alionazherdetska) with [#5968](https://github.com/swisspost/design-system/pull/5968))
    ````

### Patch Changes

-   Updated dependencies:
    -   @swisspost/design-system-components@10.0.0-next.49

-   Fixed icon loading by replacing CDN-based icon URLs with `CSS custom properties` and dynamic CSS file loading. (by [@alionazherdetska](https://github.com/alionazherdetska) with [#6214](https://github.com/swisspost/design-system/pull/6214))

author: bjornmelin
body:
This pull request introduces a major refactor to the service management and dependency injection architecture, replacing the previous bespoke FastAPI `DependencyContainer` and module-level singletons with a unified `ServiceRegistry`. The registry is now responsible for initializing and managing shared services throughout the application lifecycle, simplifying dependency management for FastAPI endpoints, CLI tooling, and tests. Additionally, the `/health` endpoint is updated to use a new health checker, returning structured JSON and HTTP status codes. The developer experience is improved with updated documentation and dev environment requirements. CLI scripts and service managers are refactored to utilize the registry, and redundant abstractions are removed.

**Service Architecture Refactor**

* Introduced `ServiceRegistry` (`src/services/registry.py`) as the central mechanism for managing shared services, replacing the previous `DependencyContainer` and singleton patterns. All FastAPI dependency helpers, CLI tooling, and lifespan events are now wired to the registry. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-06572a96a58dc510037d5efa622f9bec8519bc1beab13c9f251e97e657a9d4edR41-R43) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-828dacfa21ca442446b8837444b7a23620c3c77e44898388c17d9ecc4b72f3aaL47-R79) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-76faac66dbb870576c5e921df9ecabbab1c180f1e2e95824394f60380075bb52R1-R23)
* FastAPI endpoints and dependency helpers (`src/services/dependencies.py`, `src/api/app_factory.py`) now retrieve services via the registry, eliminating module-level locks and singletons. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-8232264e5f48b8e26e82fbbb3968eaa1d3aeb1e597af3505f6e437a0d7295ab7R11-R21) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-577a0203423d62da9efe6868c9d8e54fca1649b5d1f8621ecc1f55977b27fba3L10-L57) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-577a0203423d62da9efe6868c9d8e54fca1649b5d1f8621ecc1f55977b27fba3L87-R79) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-577a0203423d62da9efe6868c9d8e54fca1649b5d1f8621ecc1f55977b27fba3L146-R122)

**Health Endpoint and Service Initialization**

* `/health` endpoint updated to consume `ServiceHealthChecker`, returning structured JSON and HTTP status codes. Registry lifespan management is integrated into FastAPI startup/shutdown. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-8232264e5f48b8e26e82fbbb3968eaa1d3aeb1e597af3505f6e437a0d7295ab7L259-R280) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-8232264e5f48b8e26e82fbbb3968eaa1d3aeb1e597af3505f6e437a0d7295ab7R342) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-76faac66dbb870576c5e921df9ecabbab1c180f1e2e95824394f60380075bb52R1-R23)

**CLI and Service Manager Refactor**

* Vector database CLI and manager (`src/manage_vector_db.py`) now use the shared `ServiceRegistry` for initialization and cleanup, removing the need for private client managers and embedding managers. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-892868bb4f303b9265a87a8afc0aa73582919d2ebd08fe99f013da965551f999L20-R20) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-892868bb4f303b9265a87a8afc0aa73582919d2ebd08fe99f013da965551f999L65-R81) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-892868bb4f303b9265a87a8afc0aa73582919d2ebd08fe99f013da965551f999L120-R115) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-892868bb4f303b9265a87a8afc0aa73582919d2ebd08fe99f013da965551f999L343-R315)

**Developer Experience and Documentation**

* Updated documentation to describe the new registry architecture and added a TECH_DEBT note about dev environment setup requiring extras (`httpx`, `pytest-asyncio`, `asgi-lifespan`). Dev extras are now included in `pyproject.toml`. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-642395dbe6e04409397ffce7599845da44df3f79a2f7768630d6468b9122afe4R7) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-50c86b7ed8ac2cf95bd48334961bf0530cdc77b5a56f852c5c61b89d735fd711R106) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-828dacfa21ca442446b8837444b7a23620c3c77e44898388c17d9ecc4b72f3aaL47-R79)

**Testing and Configuration**

* Pytest configuration updated for deterministic test runs and quieter output; cache manager initialization logic improved for robustness. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-50c86b7ed8ac2cf95bd48334961bf0530cdc77b5a56f852c5c61b89d735fd711L355-R364) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-5fa73d46f2c2d616b17e345759fe76ea8d8b78340da0954bfc81a49fe771a77fR125-R135)

<!-- Provide a brief summary of your changes -->

**Feature Added:**
Enhanced `ResourceTemplate` URI matching and type handling logic.

## Motivation and Context

This change introduces a typed-aware URI parsing mechanism similar to FastAPI’s path parameter system.
It resolves issue **#220** by adding a more flexible and self-contained approach for handling resource URIs with type annotations.

## How Has This Been Tested?

* Verified functionality through new and existing unit tests for:

  * Typed placeholders (`{name:str}`, `{id:int}`, `{value:float}`, `{uuid:UUID}`, `{path:path}`)
  * Automatic type conversion and validation
  
* Confirmed correct parameter extraction and type enforcement in all matching scenarios.

## Breaking Changes

* None expected, but users relying on untyped string-only behaviour may observe typed conversions.

## Types of changes

* [x] New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality)


## Checklist

* [x] I have read the [[MCP Documentation](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/)](https://modelcontextprotocol.io)
* [x] My code follows the repository's style guidelines
* [x] New and existing tests pass locally
* [x] I have added appropriate error handling
* [x] I have added or updated documentation as needed

## Additional context

The implementation assumes URI templates follow a strict pattern and defaults to `str` when no type is provided.
Optional parameters and wildcard matching beyond `{path: path}` are not supported / cannot be supported.

body:
## Summary

Add Traditional Chinese (Taiwan) README and **improve installation documentation to address common installation issues** (#961, #966).

## Changes

### 1. **Improve Installation Guide** (`install/README.md`) 🔧

**Addresses Issues #961 and #966**: Many users report that the automated installation script fails. This PR provides clear alternative installation methods.

**What's New:**

- ✅ **Detailed manual installation steps** with `git clone`
- ✅ **Platform-specific instructions** (Unix/macOS/Windows)
- ✅ **Clarify directory mapping**: `ccpm/` → `.claude/`
- ✅ **Handle existing `.claude` directories** (common pain point)
- ✅ **Step-by-step Windows instructions** (cmd & PowerShell)

**Now users have a reliable fallback** when the automated script fails.

### 2. **Add Traditional Chinese README** (`README-TW.md`) 🌏

- Complete translation for Taiwan/Hong Kong users
- Includes all updates from English version
- Maintains all links and formatting

### 3. **Update Existing READMEs** 📚

- Add link to Traditional Chinese version
- Update `README.md` (English)
- Update `zh-docs/README_ZH.md` (Simplified Chinese)

## Motivation

### Problem Statement

Users frequently encounter installation failures (#961, #966, #572):

```bash
# Issue #966 - Script returns HTML instead of bash
curl -sSL https://automaze.io/ccpm/install | bash
# bash: line 8: syntax error near unexpected token `newline'
```

**Current situation:**

- Automated installation often fails
- No clear alternative documented
- Users get stuck at the first step

### Solution

**Provide clear, tested manual installation steps** that work reliably:

```bash
# New documented method that always works
git clone https://github.com/automazeio/ccpm.git temp-ccpm
cp -r temp-ccpm/ccpm .claude
rm -rf temp-ccpm
```

## Testing

### Installation Testing

- ✅ Manual installation tested on:
  - macOS (Intel & Apple Silicon)
  - Ubuntu 22.04 LTS
  - Windows 11 (PowerShell & cmd)
- ✅ Tested with existing `.claude` directory
- ✅ All markdown files render correctly
- ✅ All links functional

### Documentation Quality

- ✅ Clear section headings
- ✅ Platform-specific instructions
- ✅ Important warnings highlighted
- ✅ Next steps clearly stated

## Related Issues

- Addresses #961 - Installation errors (curl/wget failures)
- Addresses #966 - Installation error (script returns HTML)
- References #572 - Bash script issues (now provides alternative)

## Breaking Changes

None. This is purely documentation improvement.

## Additional Context

The improved installation guide ensures users can get started even when:

- Automated scripts fail due to URL redirects
- Working in an existing git repository
- Already have a `.claude` directory
- Using Windows environment

This should significantly reduce installation friction and improve the new user experience.

Linki względne do plików.

body: Heya, thanks for the plugin! This helped a lot with the load performance on one of my sites. I was running into an issue where tiles looked misaligned on my iPhone, and I realized it was because `options.doubleSize` wasn't set. Leaflet actually has a built-in property `L.Browser.retina` that reflects if it's on a retina device. This PR gives `doubleSize` that as a default, and also bumps a bunch of outdated/vulnerable dependencies. If you want to test this, you can use Firefox's responsive design mode to set the emulated device pixel ratio to 3 -- see below for screenshots of before/after this fix. Cheers 😁

author: copilot
body:
## Problem

Users encountered a **404 Not Found** error when attempting to assign barcodes to existing products from the inventory procedure. The error occurred specifically when using the "Assegna e Continua" (Assign and Continue) button in the ProductNotFoundDialog after searching for and selecting an existing product.

## Root Cause

There was a **URL endpoint mismatch** between the client service and the server controller:

- **Client** was posting to: `api/v1/product-management/product-codes`
- **Server** expected: `api/v1/product-management/products/{productId:guid}/codes`

The client was missing the `products/{productId}` portion of the path, causing the request to fail with a 404 error even though the assignment logic itself was correct.

## Solution

Updated `EventForge.Client/Services/ProductService.cs` in the `CreateProductCodeAsync` method to correctly construct the URL with the productId:

```csharp
// Before
return await _httpClientService.PostAsync<CreateProductCodeDto, ProductCodeDto>(
    "api/v1/product-management/product-codes", createDto);

// After
return await _httpClientService.PostAsync<CreateProductCodeDto, ProductCodeDto>(
    $"{BaseUrl}/{createDto.ProductId}/codes", createDto);
```

This now correctly resolves to `api/v1/product-management/products/{productId}/codes`, matching the server endpoint defined in `ProductManagementController.cs` at line 539:

```csharp
[HttpPost("products/{productId:guid}/codes")]
public async Task<ActionResult<ProductCodeDto>> AddProductCode(...)
```

## Impact

✅ Users can now successfully assign barcodes to existing products during inventory procedures  
✅ The ProductNotFoundDialog workflow completes without errors  
✅ Minimal change (1 line) reduces risk of regression  
✅ Build passes with no errors

## Testing

- Verified endpoint URL now matches server controller route pattern
- Confirmed successful build with no compilation errors
- ProductId is correctly included as a route parameter in the URL

Closes #[issue-number]

body:
# Fix Stripe webhook handler to robustly extract current_period_end

## Summary
Updates the `customer.subscription.created` webhook handler to extract `current_period_end` from the subscription items array instead of the top-level subscription object. This addresses cases where `current_period_end` is missing from the top-level subscription object but is available in the subscription items.

**Key changes:**
- Extract `current_period_end` from `subscription.items.data[0].current_period_end` 
- Remove debug logging that was cluttering logs
- Add proper error handling for missing items or missing `current_period_end` in items
- Return `current_period_end` value in success response for better debugging
- Preserve existing database operations (`create_subscription` call)

## Review & Testing Checklist for Human

**⚠️ 3 critical items to verify:**

- [ ] **Test with real Stripe webhooks**: Create a test subscription and verify the webhook payload actually contains `items.data[0].current_period_end` and that extraction works correctly
- [ ] **Verify response format compatibility**: Check that the new early return with `{"status": "success", "current_period_end": value}` doesn't break any frontend code or other consumers expecting the old response format
- [ ] **Test edge cases**: Verify error handling works for subscriptions with empty items array, items without `current_period_end`, or malformed webhook payloads

### Notes
- No existing tests cover this webhook handler, so manual testing with real Stripe webhooks is essential
- This change assumes subscription items always contain `current_period_end` - this assumption should be validated against Stripe's documentation for your specific subscription configuration
- The original issue was `current_period_end` missing from top-level subscription object, so verify this change actually resolves that problem

author: wirapratamaz
body:
This PR refactors all example files in the `/examples` directory to follow SOLID principles and clean architecture patterns, making the codebase more maintainable, testable, and easier to extend.

## Main Goals

- **ETC (Easy To Change)**: Primary focus on making code easy to modify and extend
- **SOLID Compliance**: Implement all SOLID principles throughout examples
- **Code Quality**: Eliminate code smells and improve maintainability

## Key Improvements

### Architecture Changes

- **Template Method Pattern**: Introduced `BaseExample` abstract class for consistent operation structure
- **Factory Pattern**: Added `ConfigurationFactory`, `RelayClientFactory`, and `TransactionFactory` for object creation
- **Strategy Pattern**: Implemented `ErrorHandler` with pluggable error handling strategies
- **Dependency Injection**: Proper DI for error handlers and client configuration

### New Structure

```
examples/
├── shared/
│   └── utils.ts          # Shared utilities, factories, and base classes
├── deploy.ts             # Refactored with SafeDeployer class
├── execute.ts            # Refactored with TransactionExecutor class
├── getTransaction.ts     # Refactored with TransactionRetriever class
├── getTransactions.ts    # Refactored with TransactionLister class
└── poll.ts              # Refactored with TransactionPoller class
```

### Code Smells Eliminated

- **Long Methods**: Broke down methods under 25 lines
- **Duplicate Code**: Centralized environment setup and client creation
- **Callback Hell**: Modern async/await patterns
- **Poor Error Handling**: Structured `OperationResult<T>` responses
- **Inconsistent Typing**: Replaced `any` with proper TypeScript types

## Breaking Changes

- **Method Names**: Fixed `executeSafeTransactions` → `execute` in execute.ts
- **Return Types**: All operations now return `OperationResult<T>` instead of `any`
- **Environment Setup**: Centralized in `ConfigurationFactory`

## Testing

All examples maintain the same external behavior while improving internal structure. Each example can be run independently with:

```bash
npx ts-node examples/deploy.ts
npx ts-node examples/execute.ts
# etc.
```

## 🔗 Related Issues

This improvement supports better developer experience and provides a solid foundation for future example contributions.

body: # Pull Request Description ## What does this PR change? This adds the Mute state functionality to the Participant Entries inside the Voice Chat Panel. This state is updates through the Participant Metadata from Livekit. We send a request to BE each time the user changes its microphone mute state and then BE notifies Livekit of this change, then Livekit updates the Metadata and notifies all participants. This allows for quick change of the state in all users. I also introduced a broad refactoring of the ParticipantEntry as well as several improvements to the ParticipantStateService, cleaning it up and reducing code duplication + an assortment of improvements here and there. I also fixed an issue with the settings, as it was associated with the Voice Chat FF, but we are not testing with FF but with app-args, so I added the use of FeatureId and the check of the new FeaturesRegistry on top of the old one. So we can make the change gradually. ## How to test? ### ----------> BE ON ZONE! <---------------------- * First of all, make sure you can now see the Change Microphone dropdown in the settings! This should be fixed now even without the FF enabled (just by using the proper app-args). Also, make sure that this dropdown does not appear without the app-args please 🙏 * Now the fun part, the participant entries now have more states than before (FUN), see attached image: If the participant is a SPEAKER, they can be either: * Speaking, when they are actually talking, * Muted, when they have muted the microphone * Not Speaking, but not muted, so we dont show any text or icon underneat Please check these states and make sure they are showing properly I also introduced a spinner that will show after a moderator promotes a user that Raised a Hand to speaker, until the user is properly promoted (so in between the moderator pressed the ✅ and the participant is moved to the speakers list). This spinner seems to be not spinning? I will address it afterwards as it should work 🤷 This addresses the following tickets: #5493 #5679 -> please check if you can reproduce this issue, It should be fixed, we can also check in another group voice call as it might not happen with few speakers.

author: dz24
body:
Currently it have been difficult to count the total number of subcycles actually being performed in an infretis simulation, mostly due to the "hidden"/"separately" logged WF subpaths.

Here we add a simple logger that counts the total amounts of subcycles being performed throughout an infretis simulation, stored in restart.toml.

The info in the removed pattern.txt file can technically be regenerated from the sim.log file.

# Fix CI build failures by skipping DB/Arcjet during Next build; use absolute migrations; enable PGlite in CI

## Summary
- Avoid initializing DB/PGlite and Arcjet during Next.js build-time static config collection to fix CI errors (“Aborted()”, “Failed to collect page data/configuration”).
- Use an absolute `migrations` path so Drizzle migrations resolve reliably in builds.
- Preserve existing local dev and runtime behavior. CI builds no longer require `DATABASE_URL`.
- Delete irrelevant and failing boilerplate e2e tests
- Update e2e tests to sample test cases for future reference
- Delete Checkly tests 
- Future CI tests should all pass, but any visual changes would require visual approval on visual testing third party tool, Percy

## Context
- CI failed with:
  - “Failed to collect configuration for `/[locale]` … RuntimeError: Aborted()”
  - “Failed to collect page data for `/[locale]/add`”
- Root causes:
  - Relative `./migrations` path resolved from `.next/server/...` during build.
  - Arcjet invoked during build-time.
  - Pages imported DB at module scope or used DB during build-time.

## Changes
- **DB migrations path**
  - [src/libs/DB.ts](cci:7://file:///d:/Environment/bibsnbub/src/libs/DB.ts:0:0-0:0)
    - Use `const migrationsDir = join(process.cwd(), 'migrations')`.
    - Update `migratePg`/`migratePglite` to use `migrationsDir`.
    - Import fix: `import { join } from 'node:path'`.

- **Respect `FORCE_LOCAL_DB` and refine DB selection**
  - [src/libs/DB.ts](cci:7://file:///d:/Environment/bibsnbub/src/libs/DB.ts:0:0-0:0)
    - `FORCE_LOCAL_DB` forces PGlite even if `NODE_ENV=production` (common in builds).
    - Only run Postgres migrations automatically when not production.

- **Skip Arcjet during build**
  - `src/app/[locale]/layout.tsx`
    - Guard with `process.env.NEXT_PHASE === 'phase-production-build'`.
    - Wrap in try/catch; only run Arcjet at runtime.

- **Avoid DB init during build; dynamic imports**
  - `src/app/[locale]/(add)/add/page.tsx`
    - Don’t call Supabase/DB during build; dynamically `import('@/libs/DB')` at runtime.
    - Build-time fallback returns empty arrays.
  - `src/app/[locale]/(explore)/page.tsx`
    - Guard partial local-fill; dynamic `db` import only at runtime.
    - Build-time fallback returns empty arrays.
  - `src/app/[locale]/(explore)/facility/[id]/page.tsx`
    - Remove top-level `db` import.
    - [generateStaticParams()](cci:1://file:///d:/Environment/bibsnbub/src/app/%5Blocale%5D/layout.tsx:16:0-18:1) returns `[]` during build.
    - Page uses dynamic `db` import only at runtime; build-time returns a safe fallback.

- **Env parsing**
  - [src/libs/Env.ts](cci:7://file:///d:/Environment/bibsnbub/src/libs/Env.ts:0:0-0:0): add `FORCE_LOCAL_DB` to server schema and `runtimeEnv`.

- **CI workflow fix**
  - [.github/workflows/CI.yml](cci:7://file:///d:/Environment/bibsnbub/.github/workflows/CI.yml:0:0-0:0): remove stray `]` from `SENTRY_SUPPRESS_TURBOPACK_WARNING`. Keep `FORCE_LOCAL_DB: 1`.

## Files Touched
- [src/libs/DB.ts](cci:7://file:///d:/Environment/bibsnbub/src/libs/DB.ts:0:0-0:0)
- [src/libs/Env.ts](cci:7://file:///d:/Environment/bibsnbub/src/libs/Env.ts:0:0-0:0)
- `src/app/[locale]/layout.tsx`
- `src/app/[locale]/(add)/add/page.tsx`
- `src/app/[locale]/(explore)/page.tsx`
- `src/app/[locale]/(explore)/facility/[id]/page.tsx`
- [.github/workflows/CI.yml](cci:7://file:///d:/Environment/bibsnbub/.github/workflows/CI.yml:0:0-0:0)

## Behavior Before
- Build-time attempted DB migrations and Arcjet, causing WASM aborts and path issues.
- CI build failed on `/[locale]` and `/[locale]/add`.

## Behavior After
- Build phase skips DB and Arcjet; migrations path resolves correctly.
- Local dev and runtime behaviors unchanged.
- CI build succeeds without requiring `DATABASE_URL`.

## Testing
- Local (PowerShell):
  - `$env:FORCE_LOCAL_DB='1'; $env:NODE_ENV='production'; npm run build`
  - Confirm no “Failed to collect page data/configuration” errors.
- CI:
  - Push branch; verify “Build” job passes and logs show no Arcjet/DB init during build.

## Risks
- Build-time fallbacks render with empty data for certain routes (safe); runtime fetch/DB still populates normally.
- Arcjet disabled only during build, not at runtime.

## Rollback
- Revert guarded sections in [layout.tsx](cci:7://file:///d:/Environment/bibsnbub/src/app/%5Blocale%5D/layout.tsx:0:0-0:0) and the three pages.
- Revert [src/libs/DB.ts](cci:7://file:///d:/Environment/bibsnbub/src/libs/DB.ts:0:0-0:0) to use relative `./migrations` (not recommended).

## Related Issues / Tickets

Fixes #20 

## Type of change

- [x] Fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)
- [ ] Feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)
- [ ] Refactor (no functional change)
- [x] Chore/Docs/Build
- [ ] Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to not work as expected)

## Note to Maintainers
This branch is on the women devs repo as the fork in my personal acc is being used for deployment. After this merge, all other open PRs should rebase on this branch

author: copilot
body:
## Problem

Users attempting to run the application with `docker compose up` encountered an error:

```
web-1      | Traceback (most recent call last):
web-1      |   File "/app/app.py", line 8, in <module>
web-1      |     from dotenv import load_dotenv
web-1      | ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'dotenv'
```

The root cause was that `docker-compose.yml` referenced a `.env` file that doesn't exist in the repository:

```yaml
env_file:
  - .env
```

While `.env.example` is provided as a template, the actual `.env` file is gitignored and not present after cloning. This prevented users from running the application out-of-the-box and could lead to unexpected Docker Compose behavior.

## Solution

### 1. Made `.env` file optional in `docker-compose.yml`

Commented out the `env_file` directive since all environment variables already have sensible defaults using the `${VAR:-default}` syntax:

```yaml
# Optional: Create a .env file to override default settings
# See .env.example for available configuration options
# env_file:
#   - .env
environment:
  - FLASK_ENV=${FLASK_ENV:-development}
  - MONGODB_URI=mongodb://mongodb:${MONGODB_PORT:-27017}/${MONGO_INITDB_DATABASE:-spygame}
```

### 2. Updated documentation in `README.md`

- Clarified that the `.env` file is **optional** for basic usage
- Updated "Environment Configuration" section to reflect this
- Added comprehensive "Troubleshooting" section with solutions for common Docker Compose issues, including the specific error users encountered

## Impact

**Before this fix:**
1. Clone repository
2. Must create `.env` file (or risk errors)
3. Run `docker-compose up --build`

**After this fix:**
1. Clone repository
2. Run `docker-compose up --build` ← Works immediately! 🎉
3. Optionally create `.env` to customize settings

## Testing

- ✅ Validated `docker-compose config` works without `.env` file
- ✅ Confirmed all environment variables use correct defaults
- ✅ Verified `python-dotenv`'s `load_dotenv()` handles missing `.env` gracefully
- ✅ Checked application has proper fallbacks for all configuration values

Users can now get started with the application immediately after cloning, while advanced users can still customize settings by creating a `.env` file from the provided `.env.example` template.

author: copilot
body:
## Problem

Bots were exploiting the boosted user privilege to bypass spam detection. The original middleware flow had an early return that completely skipped ALL filters (including spam checks) for boosted users, allowing malicious bots to boost the channel and post spam with immunity.

```typescript
// Before: Boosted users bypassed everything
if (isMe(ctx) || boosted || family) return; // stop processing
```

## Solution

Modified the middleware flow to check boosted users for spam while preserving their posting privileges. Now boosted users:
- ✅ **Are checked for spam** (custom emoji spam AND text spam via OpenAI classifier)
- ✅ **Retain their perks** (can post links, media, and as channels)
- ✅ **Cannot bypass detection** by simply boosting

## Changes Made

**1. Store boosted status for later middleware (lines 115-116):**
```typescript
if (isMe(ctx) || family) return; // Only these bypass all checks

ctx.state = ctx.state || {};
ctx.state.boosted = boosted;
return next();
```

**2. Preserve boosted privileges in subsequent middleware:**
- Channel bot check (line 125): `if (ctx.state?.boosted) return next();`
- Link check (line 137): `if (ctx.state?.boosted) return next();`  
- Media check (line 314): `if (ctx.state?.boosted) return;`

**3. Spam filter now runs for boosted users:**

The spam filter middleware (lines 169-196) has no boosted check, so it now runs for all boosted users. If spam is detected, the message is deleted and the user is blocked, regardless of boost status.

## Impact

### Before
```
Spam Bot → Boosts Channel → Posts Spam → ❌ Bypasses ALL checks → Spam Posted
```

### After  
```
Spam Bot → Boosts Channel → Posts Spam → ✅ Caught by spam filter → Deleted + Blocked
Legit User → Boosts Channel → Posts Message → ✅ Passes spam check → Posted Successfully
```

## Security Improvement

| User Type | Spam Check? | Can Post Links? | Can Post Media? | 
|-----------|-------------|-----------------|-----------------|
| isMe      | ❌ NO       | ✅ YES          | ✅ YES          |
| family    | ❌ NO       | ✅ YES          | ✅ YES          |
| **boosted** | **✅ YES (NEW)** | ✅ YES | ✅ YES |
| regular   | ✅ YES      | ❌ NO           | ❌ NO           |

This fix closes the security vulnerability while maintaining a good user experience for legitimate boosted users.

author: luisfabib
body:
This pull request introduces several enhancements and refactorings to the FHIR resource code generation and validation logic. The main improvements include more robust handling and serialization of function arguments for properties and validators, better import management, and improved template rendering for model fields and methods. Additionally, there are type hinting and import optimizations to support forward references and static analysis.

**Code generation improvements:**

* Added a `_cleanup_function_argument` method in `generator.py` to standardize serialization of function arguments for properties and validators, ensuring correct handling of strings and `BaseModel` instances. Closes #67.
* Enhanced property and validator extraction in `_serialize_model` to only support and process partial functions, raise clear errors for unsupported types, and collect arguments and keywords for template rendering.
* Updated the Jinja2 template (`resource_template.py.j2`) to use the new property and validator metadata, rendering arguments and keywords explicitly and supporting both field and model validators with improved clarity.

**Template and field metadata improvements:**

* Added support for including the `title` attribute in field metadata when rendering model fields in the template, improving generated code documentation. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-94922236d4a4f7816e2f3484ed2aeb8f95dfe1e37d2cd285bf95a6b36d67c4f1R35-R37) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-52687d61fd04d5327419bfa0390f69ce79f4a8f918bf135d44eaf1fe8444b272R192-R252)
* Improved error handling and validation in property and validator processing to ensure only supported function types are included in generated code.

## Overview

This PR adds a comprehensive beginner-friendly tutorial to the documentation that guides new users through creating their first simulation from scratch.

## Changes

- **New Tutorial**: 
  - Step-by-step guide for creating a first simulation
  - Complete working code examples
  - Mermaid diagrams for visualization:
    - Simulation lifecycle flow
    - Agent AI decision-making process
  - Detailed explanations of core concepts
  - Troubleshooting section

- **Updated Documentation Index**: 
  - Added new tutorial to the Tutorials section

## Tutorial Contents

### What's Covered:
- Understanding the simulation flow
- Agent personality system (8 traits explained)
- Agent archetypes (explorer, warrior, trader, crafter, hermit, bandit)
- Character classes with comparison table
- Creating and configuring agents
- Adding NPCs (enemies)
- Running simulations with visualization
- Database analysis techniques
- Advanced configuration options
- Customizing agent behavior

### Features:
- ✅ Beginner-friendly explanations
- ✅ Complete, runnable code examples
- ✅ Visual mermaid diagrams
- ✅ Practical exercises
- ✅ Troubleshooting tips
- ✅ Next steps and further reading

## Testing

- All pre-commit hooks passed
- Documentation follows existing RST format
- Properly integrated into documentation structure

## Related Issues

This tutorial bridges the gap between the quickstart guide and the more advanced tutorials, providing a hands-on walkthrough that helps new users understand core concepts while building a working simulation.

author: wesleydmscn
body:
## Sobre a solução - [x] Desafio: PIX - [x] Pasta: `submissions/wesleydmscn/pix` Stack Utilizada: TypeScript (NestJS), BullMQ, Redis, Swagger
Como rodar o projeto ## Como rodar o projeto ### Requisitos: - Node.js (versão conforme `.nvmrc`) - NVM (para gerenciar versões do Node) - Docker + Docker Compose - Redis (via container) ### Configuração de Variáveis de Ambiente: Como o sistema possui dois serviços, é necessário configurar variáveis em ambos: ```bash # Copia o exemplo de configuração para a API cp payouts-batch-api/env-example payouts-batch-api/.env # Copia o exemplo de configuração para o Worker cp payouts-batch-worker/env-example payouts-batch-worker/.env ``` ### Inicialização dos Serviços: Para iniciar o container do Redis, entre na pasta raiz `pix/` e execute: ```bash docker compose up -d ``` Para iniciar o serviço de API, entre na pasta `payouts-batch-api/` e execute: ```bash # Para rodar com a versão Node correta do projeto nvm use # Para instalar todas as dependências do serviço npm install # Para subir o servidor de desenvolvimento em http://localhost:3333 npm run start:dev ``` Para iniciar o serviço de Worker, entre na pasta `payouts-batch-worker/` e execute: ```bash # Para rodar com a versão Node correta do projeto nvm use # Para instalar todas as dependências do serviço npm install # Para subir o servidor de desenvolvimento npm run start:dev ```
## Decisões & Trade-offs - **Redis como camada de persistência temporária:** - Escolhido pela velocidade e simplicidade no armazenamento de estados em tempo real. - **Trade-off**: ausência de persistência durável, impossibilitando rastreabilidade histórica dos pagamentos. - **Separação de serviços (API e Worker):** - Permite **escalabilidade horizontal** e evita que tarefas longas impactem a performance da API. - Simula uma topologia de produção com microsserviços independentes. - **BullMQ:** - Utilizado para delegar o processamento assíncrono, com suporte nativo a **retries**, **delays**, **prioridades**, **concorrência configurável** e **monitoramento** via UI. - Facilita a adição futura de mecanismos como **dead letter queues** e **rate limiting** por job. - **Observabilidade limitada:** - Atualmente, o sistema conta apenas com **logs estruturados**. - Futuras melhorias incluem métricas com **Prometheus** e tracing distribuído com **OpenTelemetry**. ### O que faria diferente com mais tempo - Implementaria testes automatizados (unitários e de integração) com **Jest** e **Supertest**; - Adicionaria camada de persistência **PostgreSQL** para histórico de pagamentos e auditoria; - Expandiria o conjunto de endpoints para permitir relatórios detalhados de todos os lotes; - Incluiria monitoramento e observabilidade com **Prometheus + Grafana**; - Melhoraria a **gestão de configuração** e **secrets**, integrando variáveis de ambiente com **Vault** ou **AWS Parameter Store**. ## Evidências | API em Produção: https://conty-challenge.wesleydmscn.com/docs | |--------| | |

# Comprehensive Test Coverage Expansion

## 📋 Summary

This PR implements a comprehensive test coverage expansion for the `unilink` library, adding 74 new tests across 8 categories to ensure enterprise-grade quality and reliability. The implementation includes boundary testing, error recovery testing, stress testing, configuration validation, and performance benchmarking.

## 🎯 Objectives

- **Expand test coverage** from basic functionality to comprehensive quality assurance
- **Implement systematic testing** across multiple categories and scenarios
- **Ensure enterprise-grade reliability** through thorough validation
- **Provide performance benchmarks** for optimization and regression detection
- **Validate error handling** and recovery mechanisms

## 🚀 Key Features

### 1. **Boundary Testing** (`test_boundary.cc`)
- Memory pool boundary conditions and edge cases
- Configuration validation for TCP client/server and serial
- Transport layer boundary testing
- Backpressure threshold validation

### 2. **Error Recovery Testing** (`test_error_recovery.cc`)
- Network connection error scenarios
- Serial port error handling
- Retry mechanism validation
- Exception safety testing
- Memory allocation failure handling
- Resource cleanup verification

### 3. **Stress Testing** (`test_stress.cc`)
- High-load memory pool operations
- Concurrent access performance
- Memory leak detection
- Long-running stability testing
- High-frequency data transmission simulation

### 4. **Configuration Validation** (`test_config_validation.cc`)
- TCP client/server configuration validation

## Summary

This PR systematically eliminates all barrel files from the core package and consolidates pure utilities into the shared package for better modularity and reusability.

## Changes

### 1. Removed All Barrel Files ✅
- **Deleted** `packages/core/src/index.ts` (main barrel export)
- **Renamed** all remaining `index.ts` files to explicit module names:
  - `core-config/index.ts` → `core-config/coreConfig.ts`
  - `mutations/index.ts` → `mutations/MutationCoordinator.ts`
  - `summaries/index.ts` → `summaries/createSummary.ts`
  - `workflow/index.ts` → `workflow/verifyWorkflow.ts`

### 2. Enhanced Package Exports ✅
Updated `packages/core/package.json` to include comprehensive wildcard exports:
- **Added:** `./evaluation/*`, `./improvement/*`, `./node/*`, `./tools/*`
- **Updated:** `./core-config` to point to explicit file path

### 3. Moved Stateless Utilities to @lucky/shared ✅
Migrated pure, reusable utilities from core to shared package:
- `genShortId()` → `@lucky/shared` (crypto-based ID generation)
- `asArray()` → `@lucky/shared` (array coercion utility)
- `withDescriptions()` → `@lucky/shared` (Zod schema helper)

Updated both main and client exports in @lucky/shared. Fixed TypeScript compilation by adding DOM lib for crypto API.

- **53 files changed** across the monorepo
- **~96 import statements** changed to use explicit file paths
- Updated imports in core package, web app, and test files

✅ **Cleaner Architecture**: Explicit wildcard exports eliminate barrel file complexity  
✅ **Better Modularity**: Pure utilities now centralized in shared package  
✅ **Improved Reusability**: Stateless functions accessible across all packages  
✅ **Reduced Coupling**: Core package focused on orchestration, not utilities

body:
### What is the context of this PR?

We originally didn't include the `KAFKA_SERVERS` config in the `dev.py` settings file and left it for the developer to configure it for themselves in their environment via `local.py`, `.env`, etc.

The recent change: https://github.com/ONSdigital/dis-wagtail/pull/379 means now the `dev.py` defaults to using our Kafka broker container locally for local development purposes.

It would make sense to set the `KAFKA_SERVERS` config in `dev.py` as well; otherwise, by default, the config isn't set and there will be issues when publishing, unpublishing and deleting pages (if not set in the environment already, such as manually overriding it in the `settings files`, `local.py` etc or having it in `.env`)

### How to review

- Don't set any Kafka server config in your local environment, such as `local.py`, `.env`, make sure not to have any of the `settings files` overriden already, such as `base` settings.
- You must be able to publish, unpublish and delete pages without issues, and see the logs when it's successful when Kafka returns the record metadata.

Credit to @AdamHawtin for discovering and informing me of this issue =)

List any follow-up actions (if applicable), like needed documentation updates or additional testing.

This pull request refactors and improves several core simulation and testing components, focusing on simplifying documentation, updating network fault modeling, enhancing buggify (fault injection) logic, and cleaning up assertion code. The changes increase clarity, maintainability, and accuracy of simulation behaviors.

**Network Fault Modeling Updates:**

* Refactored `NetworkConfiguration` to distinguish between clogging and partition faults, replacing the previous generic fault fields with more precise `clog_probability`, `clog_duration`, `partition_probability`, and `partition_duration` fields. Updated all relevant default and random configuration logic to use these new fields. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-18bd458ecf6e17cea11031e849ae96c441b750c8820675de684b5c57e05a1fe2L19-R27) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-18bd458ecf6e17cea11031e849ae96c441b750c8820675de684b5c57e05a1fe2L35-R41) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-18bd458ecf6e17cea11031e849ae96c441b750c8820675de684b5c57e05a1fe2L69-R78)

**Buggify System Improvements:**

* Rewrote the buggify (deterministic fault injection) module to simplify its API and internal state, remove single-fire behavior, and clarify activation/firing logic. Improved deterministic behavior and activation consistency in tests. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-2eab2969e62760298664f55d69dd5f63b1f174a61ce052469f1fffbd65d14029L1-R72) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-2eab2969e62760298664f55d69dd5f63b1f174a61ce052469f1fffbd65d14029L181-R114) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-2eab2969e62760298664f55d69dd5f63b1f174a61ce052469f1fffbd65d14029L228-R132)

**Simulation Event Infrastructure:**

* Expanded `ConnectionStateChange` enum to include explicit partition and partition-clear events, and updated infrastructure event detection and tests accordingly. **Assertion and Documentation Cleanup:**

* Removed in-source example code from assertion and simulation documentation, replacing with concise descriptions. Simplified assertion macro docs and improved clarity of assertion statistics APIs. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-02325290d5d65cbab342c6eed8357a51d7f06c177b8983e23862c5770bb89363L36-R36) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-02325290d5d65cbab342c6eed8357a51d7f06c177b8983e23862c5770bb89363L103-R93) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-02325290d5d65cbab342c6eed8357a51d7f06c177b8983e23862c5770bb89363L129-R103) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-02325290d5d65cbab342c6eed8357a51d7f06c177b8983e23862c5770bb89363L193-R155) [[5]](diffhunk://#diff-02325290d5d65cbab342c6eed8357a51d7f06c177b8983e23862c5770bb89363L234-R185) [[6]](diffhunk://#diff-02325290d5d65cbab342c6eed8357a51d7f06c177b8983e23862c5770bb89363L278-R218) [[7]](diffhunk://#diff-27b9895736b00d12293c5fbe233179890757714af9cdd021cb90f82b18c0031bL13-R13)

body:
##### SUMMARY
This PR contains 3 items that needed to be fixed in order for me to run the module in the same manner as I was before the current version of the collection. 

1. Without `current_state.copy()` on `new_state = current_state`, you will be updating `current_state` every time you change `new_state` so changes will never be pushed due to `if new_state != current_state:`.

2. The logic for validating `servicelist` argument was broken as the code tried to sort a bool. 

3. Also, if you are not providing an address then `elif valid_ipv4(new_state["address"]):` will fail so you need to validate an address is provided beforehand. 

##### ISSUE TYPE
- Bugfix Pull Request

##### COMPONENT NAME
plugins/modules/purefa_network.py

##### ADDITIONAL INFORMATION
This was required in order to make changes to servicelist without an address on the physical interface.
Example:
```
- name: Configure and enable iSCSI network interfaces
  purestorage.flasharray.purefa_network:
    name: "{{ item }}"
    mtu: 9000
    servicelist:
      - iscsi
    state: present
    fa_url: "{{ mgmt_vip }}"
    api_token: "{{ token }}"
  delegate_to: localhost
  loop: "{{ iscsi_ports }}"
```

author: weareaisle-demo-app[bot]
body:
This patch addresses a command injection vulnerability in the Docker container terminal WebSocket server. The vulnerability exists because user-controlled input (`containerId` and `activeWay`) is directly interpolated into command strings without proper validation at lines 58 and 110.

Changes made:

1. Added constants at the top level of the file:
   - `CONTAINER_ID_PATTERN`: A regex pattern to validate Docker container IDs
   - `ALLOWED_COMMANDS`: A whitelist of permitted shell commands

2. Implemented a `validateDockerParams` function that:
   - Validates that container ID exists and matches the expected pattern
   - Validates that the command exists and is in the allowed commands list
   - Returns validation status and error message if validation fails

3. Replaced the simple existence check with comprehensive validation:
   - Uses the validation function to check both containerId and activeWay parameters
   - Closes the connection with an appropriate error message if validation fails

The fix effectively prevents command injection by ensuring that:
- Container IDs can only contain alphanumeric characters, underscores, and hyphens
- Commands are restricted to a predefined whitelist of safe shell commands

These changes maintain the original functionality while adding proper input validation to prevent malicious command injection.

author: copilot
body:
## Problem

The CI/CD pipeline was failing with the following error during the Docker image attestation step:

```
Error: Failed to get ID token: Error message: Unable to get ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_URL env variable
```

## Root Cause

The `actions/attest-build-provenance@v1` action requires the `id-token: write` permission to generate OIDC tokens for creating build attestations. The `docker` job in the workflow was missing this required permission, causing the action to fail when attempting to request an ID token from GitHub's token service.

## Solution

Added the `id-token: write` permission to the `docker` job's permissions configuration in `.github/workflows/ci-cd.yml`:

```yaml
permissions:
  contents: read
  packages: write
  id-token: write  # Added this line
```

This allows the workflow to:
- Request OIDC tokens from GitHub's token service
- Successfully generate build provenance attestations
- Push attestations to the container registry alongside Docker images

## Changes

- Added `id-token: write` permission to the docker job in `.github/workflows/ci-cd.yml`

The change follows GitHub's principle of least privilege by explicitly declaring only the permissions required for the job to function correctly.

Fixes the build error reported in the issue.

author: gpunto
body:
### Goal

[AND-801](https://linear.app/stream/issue/AND-801/update-sample-to-use-the-timeline-group-instead-of-user-for-the)

We've been using the user feed group wrong. `user:user_id` feeds are supposed to only contain the user's own posts and they should not follow other feeds. Instead, we should display `timeline:user_id` and have it follow user feeds.

### Implementation

- Use 2 different `Feed` instances: one with `timeline` group to display timeline & stories (which are still part of the timeline) and one with `user` group to post user's activities
- Make `timeline:user_x` auto follow `user:user_x`, otherwise the timeline wouldn't show the user's own posts
- Use a `Feed` with `user` group when querying follow suggestions, because we want to follow `user` feeds, not `timeline` ones
- Simplify args to avoid passing feed/user ID when not needed

### Testing

Launch the sample and verify everything works: interacting with the feed, follow/unfollow, notifications, etc.

Note: some follow relationship we had before might not exist after these changes, because they were like `user:user_x ->  user:user_y`, while now we have `timeline:user_x -> user:user_y`.

author: shipilev
body:
During the performance investigations in safepoint machinery (notably [JDK-8350324](https://bugs.openjdk.org/browse/JDK-8350324)), I found the trace logging lacking. It would be good to improve it in order to finely profile various microscopic things like thread list walks, the blocking/resuming of Java threads, etc. For [JDK-8350324](https://bugs.openjdk.org/browse/JDK-8350324), for example, I want to be able to measure the Java thread delays if they assist in avalanche wakeups. This leans heavily on unified logging and invariant clocks to do the right thing, but I think it is a fair compromise for simplicity. The configuration I found most useful for testing is: ``` -Xlog:async -Xlog:safepoint=trace:file=safepoint.log:uptimenanos ``` My tentative plan is to visualize this more comprehensively with a little tool that digests that log. I am open for bikeshedding on logging wording. The log example is in the comment below. author: isakstenstrom
body:
Make the footer configurable by using environment variables for the frontend.

The footer is configured with the `NEXT_PUBLIC_FOOTER_CONTENT_JSON` environment variable that expects an array of footer items. Each item should have the following properties:

- `text`: The text that the item should have.
- `href`: The url to where the item leads when clicked.
- `icon`: The icon to be used next to the text. It can either be `slack`, `github`, or `discord` (the appropriate icons that existed in the icon library used in the frontend), or a url to a icon, or it can be left omitted to leave the icon without icon. 

The default is left to the old default, i.e. the link to the BuildTeamWorld slack.

author: trevnels-cs
body:
Login page - directs users to SSO login, while also allowing "expo login" for standard user accounts using our own login endpoint.

Adds a basic RequireUser wrapper component that allows routes to redirect unauthenticated users to the login page.

Adds user name to the NavBar when logged in, and switches between Log In and Log Out in the profile dropdown depending on auth state.

Note that login/logout must perform browser navigation (doing a full refresh) instead of using react-router, since the csrfToken in window.init has to be updated when auth changes.

author: kyllianchandelier
body:
This pull request introduces user authentication features to the web client, including both traditional login/signup and Google OAuth integration. It also updates the UI to support these flows and refines layout components for consistency.

### Authentication features

* Added new `Login` and `Signup` pages with forms for username/password authentication, error handling, and auto-login after signup. Both pages also support Google OAuth login using the `@react-oauth/google` package.
* Integrated Google OAuth provider into the app's routing structure, enabling Google login functionality for authentication flows.
* Added dependencies for authentication and API communication: `@react-oauth/google`, `axios`, `jwt-decode`, and `react-auth-kit`.

### Routing and navigation

* Updated routing to include `/login` and `/signup` paths for the new authentication pages.

## Pull Request type

<!-- Please try to limit your pull request to one type; submit multiple pull requests if needed. -->

Please add the labels corresponding to the type of changes your PR introduces:

## What is the current behavior?

Currently, No batching happens for L3s. PIEs/Proofs are created for individual blocks.

<!-- Please describe the current behavior that you are modifying, or link to a relevant issue. -->

Resolves: #NA

## What is the new behavior?

<!-- Please describe the behavior or changes that are being added by this PR. -->

Updated the batching worker to create SNOS batches in case of L3s

### Batching Worker

Batching worker works differently for L2s and L3s

For L2s, we create both aggregator and snos batches.
Snos batches are then used by the snos job to create PIEs for batches instead of single blocks.
Aggregator batches (which essentially contains multiple snos batches and hence many blocks)
are used in proof creation job to create a single aggregator pie and a single proof which is
then registered on chain and the state update can be done for multiple blocks at once.

For L3s, we create only the snos batch.
Snos jobs are created for the generated snos batches.
Then these PIEs are sent for proof generation and registration on chain.
Finally, we can do the state update for multiple blocks (which are present in the snos batch)
at once.

## Does this introduce a breaking change?

Yes

author: gmarler
body:
Depending on whether your editor uses `clang-format` or not to reformat certain code files (mine does), if you don't have a sensible configuration for `clang-format`, you might end up with breaking changes in your eBPF code - like reordering includes.

This PR adds sensible defaults, particularly `SortIncludes: 'false'`, although @javierhonduco may want to make changes to indent widths and the like.

This file is local to the `src/bpf/` directory.  Noticing that there isn't one for the top level directory, which should probably be rectified as well.

I've tested this against most of the BPF files, and it has prevented breaking changes, as well as kept most of the formatting the way it is.

body:
Olá Priscylla,

Envio esta correção para o bug onde o Mario continuava se movendo ou "caindo" para o chão após a colisão, mesmo com o Game Over ativo.

### Solução Aplicada:

O problema era que a animação CSS do pulo continuava sendo executada após a colisão. Para resolver, fiz o seguinte na função `gameOver()`:

1.  **Parada Imediata:** Removi a classe `jump` e cancelei a animação (`mario.style.animation = 'none';`) para parar o movimento no instante exato da batida.
2.  **Fixação de Posição:** Capturei a posição vertical precisa (`marioPosition`) no momento da morte e a fixei com `mario.style.bottom`. Isso impede qualquer movimento residual ou que o Mario "teleporte" para a posição `bottom: 0`.

Obrigado pelo projeto. Foi um ótimo exercício!

body:
On Mac OS X version 14 or earlier there seems to be a crash when closing the PowerPoint. This could be due to incorrect order of cleaning up the observer.

<!--- See CONTRIBUTING.md for general guidelines on contributions -->

## What does the pull request do?
In `OverlayWindowImpl` the FirstResponderObserver object is released in the destructor. `FirstResponderObserver` destructor removes the registered observer. But `OverlayWindowImpl` destructor removes the view before  `FirstResponderObserver` is released.  So view may point to invalid window at the time of removing the observer and it could potentially lead to crash.

This PR fixes the order of releasing the objects.

## What is the current behavior?
PowerPoint may crash while closing the presentation (may be on Mac OS X version 14 or earlier).


## What is the updated/expected behavior with this PR?
PowerPoint should not crash while closing the presentation.

body:
## Overview

This PR implements a comprehensive Test Planning & Quality Assurance Framework to standardize test planning, quality validation, and GitHub project management across all features. The framework is built on industry-standard methodologies including ISTQB (International Software Testing Qualifications Board) and ISO 25010 quality standards.

## What's New

### Documentation Structure (6 files, 3,509 lines)

A complete documentation hierarchy has been created under `docs/`:

- **`docs/README.md`** - Main documentation index with quick start guides for different roles (Project Managers, QA Engineers, Developers, Product Owners)
- **`docs/ways-of-work/README.md`** - Framework overview explaining principles of standardization, quality focus, risk management, and continuous improvement
- **`docs/ways-of-work/plan/README.md`** - Comprehensive 482-line guide covering the complete framework usage, ISTQB techniques, ISO 25010 characteristics, quality gates, and best practices
- **`docs/ways-of-work/plan/example-epic/example-feature/test-strategy.md`** - 457-line template for creating test strategies with ISTQB test design techniques and ISO 25010 quality assessment
- **`docs/ways-of-work/plan/example-epic/example-feature/test-issues-checklist.md`** - 711-line comprehensive checklist for breaking down test tasks by level (Unit, Integration, E2E, Performance, Security, Accessibility, Regression)
- **`docs/ways-of-work/plan/example-epic/example-feature/qa-plan.md`** - 842-line quality assurance plan template with 7-gate quality framework, metrics, and validation procedures

### GitHub Issue Templates (3 files, 513 lines)

Three standardized issue templates to streamline test task creation:

- **`.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/test-strategy.md`** - Template for creating test strategy issues with ISTQB framework application, ISO 25010 quality characteristic assessment, and quality gates
- **`.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/playwright-test.md`** - Template for Playwright E2E test implementation with Page Object Model guidance, test case design, accessibility testing (WCAG Level AA default), and CI/CD integration
- **`.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/quality-assurance.md`** - Template for overall quality validation with ISO 25010 assessment, quality gate validation, test metrics, and release readiness criteria

## Framework Components

### ISTQB Framework Implementation

The framework includes comprehensive guidance on applying ISTQB test design techniques:

- **Equivalence Partitioning** - Input domain partitioning into valid/invalid classes
- **Boundary Value Analysis** - Edge case identification and testing
- **Decision Table Testing** - Complex business rule validation
- **State Transition Testing** - System state behavior validation
- **Experience-Based Testing** - Exploratory and error guessing approaches

Test types coverage includes Functional, Non-Functional, Structural, and Change-Related testing with clear guidelines for each.

### ISO 25010 Quality Model

Complete coverage of all 8 quality characteristics with assessment templates:

1. **Functional Suitability** - Completeness, correctness, appropriateness validation
2. **Performance Efficiency** - Time behavior, resource utilization, capacity testing
3. **Compatibility** - Co-existence and interoperability validation
4. **Usability** - Accessibility (WCAG Level AA), learnability, operability
5. **Reliability** - Fault tolerance, recoverability, availability testing
6. **Security** - Confidentiality, integrity, authentication, authorization validation
7. **Maintainability** - Modularity, reusability, testability assessment
8. **Portability** - Adaptability, installability, replaceability validation

### 7-Gate Quality Framework

A structured approach to quality validation throughout the development lifecycle:

1. **Requirements Quality Gate** - Requirements completeness and testability
2. **Design Quality Gate** - Architecture and design validation
3. **Implementation Quality Gate** - Code quality and unit testing (≥80% coverage)
4. **Integration Quality Gate** - Component integration validation
5. **System Testing Quality Gate** - E2E, performance, security, accessibility testing
6. **UAT Quality Gate** - User acceptance and business validation
7. **Production Readiness Gate** - Final release criteria validation

Each gate includes entry criteria, validation steps, exit criteria, quality metrics, and escalation procedures.

### Test Coverage Targets

Clear, measurable coverage targets:

- **Code Coverage**: ≥80% line coverage, ≥90% branch coverage for critical paths
- **Functional Coverage**: 100% acceptance criteria validation
- **Risk Coverage**: 100% high-risk scenarios, ≥90% medium-risk, ≥70% low-risk
- **Quality Characteristics**: All applicable ISO 25010 characteristics validated

### GitHub Integration

Standardized approach to test task management:

- **Labels**: Consistent taxonomy for test types (`unit-test`, `e2e-test`, `performance-test`, etc.), quality frameworks (`istqb`, `iso25010`), priorities (`test-critical`, `test-high`), and components (`frontend-test`, `backend-test`)
- **Task Estimation**: Clear guidelines by test type (Unit: 0.5-1 SP, Integration: 1-2 SP, E2E: 2-3 SP, Performance: 3-5 SP, Security: 2-4 SP)
- **Risk-Based Prioritization**: Critical/High/Medium/Low priority assignment based on risk assessment

🚨 Your current dependencies have known security vulnerabilities 🚨 This dependency update fixes known security vulnerabilities. Please see the details below and assess their impact carefully. We recommend to merge and deploy this as soon as possible!
Here is everything you need to know about this update. Please take a good look at what changed and the test results before merging this pull request. ### What changed? #### ↗️ rack (_indirect_, 2.0.7 → 2.2.19) · [Repo](https://github.com/rack/rack) · [Changelog](https://github.com/rack/rack/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md)
Security Advisories 🚨

🚨 Rack's multipart parser buffers unbounded per-part headers, enabling DoS (memory exhaustion)

Summary

Rack::Multipart::Parser can accumulate unbounded data when a multipart part’s header block never terminates with the required blank line (CRLFCRLF). The parser keeps appending incoming bytes to memory without a size cap, allowing a remote attacker to exhaust memory and cause a denial of service (DoS).

Details

While reading multipart headers, the parser waits for CRLFCRLF using:

@sbuf.scan_until(/(.*?\r\n)\r\n/m)

If the terminator never appears, it continues appending data (@sbuf.concat(content)) indefinitely. There is no limit on accumulated header bytes, so a single malformed part can consume memory proportional to the request body size.

Impact

Attackers can send incomplete multipart headers to trigger high memory use, leading to process termination (OOM) or severe slowdown. The effect scales with request size limits and concurrency. All applications handling multipart uploads may be affected.

Mitigation

  • Upgrade to a patched Rack version that caps per-part header size (e.g., 64 KiB).
  • Until then, restrict maximum request sizes at the proxy or web server layer (e.g., Nginx client_max_body_size).

🚨 Rack's unbounded multipart preamble buffering enables DoS (memory exhaustion)

Summary

Rack::Multipart::Parser buffers the entire multipart preamble (bytes before the first boundary) in memory without any size limit. A client can send a large preamble followed by a valid boundary, causing significant memory use and potential process termination due to out-of-memory (OOM) conditions.

Details

While searching for the first boundary, the parser appends incoming data into a shared buffer (@sbuf.concat(content)) and scans for the boundary pattern:

@sbuf.scan_until(@body_regex)

If the boundary is not yet found, the parser continues buffering data indefinitely. There is no trimming or size cap on the preamble, allowing attackers to send arbitrary amounts of data before the first boundary.

Impact

Remote attackers can trigger large transient memory spikes by including a long preamble in multipart/form-data requests. The impact scales with allowed request sizes and concurrency, potentially causing worker crashes or severe slowdown due to garbage collection.

Mitigation

  • Upgrade: Use a patched version of Rack that enforces a preamble size limit (e.g., 16 KiB) or discards preamble data entirely per RFC 2046 § 5.1.1.
  • Workarounds:
    • Limit total request body size at the proxy or web server level.
    • Monitor memory and set per-process limits to prevent OOM conditions.

🚨 Rack: Multipart parser buffers large non‑file fields entirely in memory, enabling DoS (memory exhaustion)

Summary

Rack::Multipart::Parser stores non-file form fields (parts without a filename) entirely in memory as Ruby String objects. A single large text field in a multipart/form-data request (hundreds of megabytes or more) can consume equivalent process memory, potentially leading to out-of-memory (OOM) conditions and denial of service (DoS).

Details

During multipart parsing, file parts are streamed to temporary files, but non-file parts are buffered into memory:

body = String.new  # non-file → in-RAM buffer
@mime_parts[mime_index].body << content

There is no size limit on these in-memory buffers. As a result, any large text field—while technically valid—will be loaded fully into process memory before being added to params.

Impact

Attackers can send large non-file fields to trigger excessive memory usage. Impact scales with request size and concurrency, potentially leading to worker crashes or severe garbage-collection overhead. All Rack applications processing multipart form submissions are affected.

Mitigation

  • Upgrade: Use a patched version of Rack that enforces a reasonable size cap for non-file fields (e.g., 2 MiB).
  • Workarounds:
    • Restrict maximum request body size at the web-server or proxy layer (e.g., Nginx client_max_body_size).
    • Validate and reject unusually large form fields at the application level.

author: sirtyson
body:
# Description

Removes a faulty optimization in `getNewestVersion`.

Previously, whenever all buckets had an in-memory cache, we didn't use the LTX cache and instead queried directly from the BucketListDB cache. Prior to p23, this was fine. However, this is no longer optimal. The BucketList level cache is made up of 21 maps, so searching is much more expensive than the single soroban state cache or the LTX random eviction cache. We bypassed both the LTX and soroban cache, favoring the most expensive DB level cache. This removes the bypass.

It also disables meta for max TPS testing, which seems reasonable given that validators don't emit meta, and watcher nodes don't participate in consensus and can have longer apply times without losing sync. 

Rebased on https://github.com/stellar/stellar-core/pull/4952.

## Summary Fixes #207 by removing the legacy interactive prompting feature that was causing the tool to crash when run without proper configuration. The tool now provides clear, actionable error messages instead of prompting users for partial configuration. ## Problem The Data Migration Tool had legacy interactive behavior that would: 1. Prompt users to select source/sink from a numbered list if not specified 2. Prompt for settings file path if not found 3. Crash with an exception after prompting because other required settings were missing This created a confusing user experience as shown in the issue - users would select "15 SqlServer" as source and "3 Cosmos-nosql" as sink, only to have the tool crash because connection strings and other required settings weren't configured. ## Solution Removed all interactive prompting and added proper validation that fails fast with helpful error messages: ### When `migrationsettings.json` is missing: ``` Error: Settings file 'migrationsettings.json' not found. Please provide a valid settings file or specify --source and --sink options. Use --help for more information. ``` ### When Source/Sink are not configured: ``` Error: Invalid configuration. Both Source and Sink must be specified. The settings file 'migrationsettings.json' is missing required Source or Sink values. Please provide valid Source and Sink in the settings file or via command line arguments. Use --help for more information. ``` ### When extension name is invalid: ``` Source extension 'invalid-name' not found. Use 'dmt list' to see available extensions. ``` ## Changes - **RunCommand.cs**: - Added validation in `InvokeAsync` to check for missing settings file and incomplete configuration - Removed interactive prompting loop from `GetExtensionSelection` - Removed settings file path prompting from `BuildSettingsConfiguration` - All methods now throw clear exceptions or return error codes with helpful messages - **RunCommandTests.cs**: Added 5 new test cases to validate the new behavior ## Testing - ✅ All existing tests continue to pass (no breaking changes to valid configurations) - ✅ 5 new test cases validate error handling for invalid configurations - ✅ Manual testing verified all error scenarios display helpful messages - ✅ Tool works correctly when proper configuration is provided via settings file or command-line arguments ## Benefits 1. **Clearer UX**: Users get immediate, actionable feedback instead of being prompted for incomplete configuration 2. **Better error messages**: Guidance to use `--help` and `dmt list` commands 3. **Fail fast**: Tool exits with error code 1 and clear message instead of prompting and crashing 4. **Consistent with modern CLI tools**: No interactive prompts, all configuration via files or arguments ## Breaking Changes This removes the interactive prompting behavior. Users who relied on being prompted to select source/sink will need to specify them via: - Command-line: `dmt --source json --sink cosmos-nosql ...` - Settings file: Properly configured `migrationsettings.json` However, the old interactive behavior would crash anyway after prompting, so this change improves the user experience for all scenarios.

We should no longer prompt the user and instead if the tool is run without arguments and the migrationsettings.json in the current directory is invalid we should indicate to the user it's invalid and then display the help information. If no migrationsettings.json is present the help should be displayed. author: vakarian-s
body: # Add player and Entity Introduce Entity/Player systems, lifespan & expiry callbacks, aim-aligned shooting, and Scene0g bullet/effect management ## Summary This PR introduces a minimal entity system (Entity, Player), adds lifespan + expiry callback mechanics, implements aim rendering and shooting aligned to the player’s crosshairs, and updates Scene0g to own/render players, bullets, and transient effects. It also wires up sprite renderers and input for A/D rotation and SPACE to shoot. ## Context / Problem - We needed a base entity abstraction (position, scale, orientation) to unify update/render transforms. - Bullets and other short-lived objects need a simple, explicit lifespan and a way to notify the scene at expiry. - Crosshair visual and bullet spawn point weren’t aligned; model matrix math/order had to be nailed down. - Scene0g required ownership of spawned objects and safe removal on expiry. ## What’s Changed ### Project structure / build Added: - `include/Entities/Entity.h` - `include/Entities/Player.h` - `src/Entities/Entity.cpp` - `src/Entities/Player.cpp`. - `vcxproj`: new ClCompile items for Entity.cpp and Player.cpp with per-file settings; added ClIncludes for new headers; extended include paths (absolute paths for imgui and include/). ### Core: Entity - Position/scale/orientation and GetModelMatrix (T * R * S). - Lifespan API: `SetLifeSpan(…)`, `IsExpired()`, `IsImmortal(`), `GetCurrentLifeTime()`. - Expiry callbacks: virtual OnExpired() plus external `SetExpiredCallback(std::function)`, fired exactly once on transition to expired. - `Update(deltaTime)` accrues time and triggers the above hooks. ### Gameplay: Player - Stores `crossHairsDirection` (quaternion), `crossHairsScale`, `crossHairsOffset`. - `MoveAim(angleInDegrees)`: rotates crosshairs around Z via `QMath::angleAxisRotation`. - Aim model matrix: T * R * L * S (translation * rotation * local offset * scale) so offset is in world units (no scale bleed). - `Shoot()`: spawns a bullet entity at the exact world position of the crosshair via TRL * (0,0,0,1), sets 2s lifespan, returns std::unique_ptr to the caller. ### Scene: Scene0g #### Ownership: - `std::vector> players` - `std::vector> bullets` - `std::vector> effects` #### Input: - A/D rotates crosshairs (MoveAim(±2°) per frame while held). - SPACE fires: scene receives unique_ptr, attaches expired callback to spawn an impact effect, then stores bullet. #### Update loop: - Update all players/bullets/effects. - Erase-remove any expired items from each container. #### Rendering: - Sets up sprite renderers for player, crosshairs, bullets, impact; renders each container with its model matrix. #### Assets: - Updated textures: fist.png, idle.png, crosshairs.png, impact.png. ## Implementation Notes - Expiry model: The base class triggers OnExpired() and the external callback once; the scene only prunes in its normal erase/remove pass (no mid-iteration deletion). - Ownership: All spawned entities use `std::unique_ptr`. No shared ownership is needed; lifetimes are governed by the scene containers. ## Testing 1. Launch Scene0g. 2. Hold A or D to rotate the crosshairs; observe crosshair rotation around the player. 3. Press SPACE: 4. A bullet appears exactly at the crosshair position and moves/animates with its transform. 5. After ~2 seconds, the bullet expires and triggers the expired callback: 6. An impact effect spawns at the bullet’s last position. 7. Allow both bullet and effect to expire; verify they are removed from their respective vectors (no leaks/crashes). ## Screenshots

author: kayakincoder
body:
## Related issue(s)

SNS and S3 are common event sources for Cirrus Payloads. This feature provides a config-driven means to feed those event sources to the Cirrus Process Queue.

## Proposed Changes

1. A `cirrus_inputs.feeder_definitions_dir` option to denote a directory containing N number of subdirectories, each of which defines a feeder (similar to `cirrus_inputs.task_definitions_dir`). For example:

```
/cirrus
    /feeders
        /feeder1
            definition.yaml
        /feeder2
            definition.yaml
```

Each `definition.yaml` creates:

- N number of SNS and/or S3 triggers
  - Note that this module does not *create* SNS topics or S3 buckets. Rather, it provides a way to generate the necessary AWS permissions and resources for *existing* topics and/or buckets to trigger messages to an SQS queue
- A single SQS queue to receive messages from those trigger(s)
- A single lambda function to read messages from that SQS queue, process them, and send them to the Cirrus Process Queue

See `/modules/cirrus/cirrus-examples/feeders` and `/modules/cirrus/feeder/README.md` for more detail

2. Additionally, a submodule `/modules/cirrus/feeder/lambda` was created as a *potential* for DRY-ing up task + feeder lambda creation. Both tasks and feeders require (quite involved) lambda creation; a single lambda module that both can use is the future hope.

**Note**: Feeders should be considered as being in beta, not production-ready quite yet. A few remaining tasks items will be buttoned up in a future PR:

- Full SSM support. See `feeder_task_workflow.tf` todo
- Detailed documentation in `/modules/cirrus/cirrus-examples/feeders`

## Testing

This change was validated by the following observations:

1. Build FilmDrop with `feeder_definitions_dir = null` to ensure no changes to existing behavior
2. Build FilmDrop with `feeder_definitions_dir = /somedir` and various feeder configuration options to validate expected feeder behavior
